messages.text: been arguing a lot with my wife lately

It sounds like things have been really tough between you and your wife recently. Frequent conflict can be emotionally draining for everyone involved. Could you share a bit more about what these arguments are typically about? How is this situation affecting your mood or daily life right now?
she's always snapping at me, like everything I say is wrong

It sounds incredibly frustrating to feel like your words are constantly being dismissed. That kind of criticism can make anyone feel defensive or unheard. How does that dynamic make you feel when it happens? Have you tried to discuss this pattern with her when things are calm?
it's not about feelings. i just need to know how to stop it from turning into a fight every time

I understand you are looking for concrete strategies to de-escalate these situations rather than focusing on emotions right now. One effective approach is to take a structured time-out when you notice the tension rising, ideally after agreeing on a signal beforehand. You might also try using "I" statements to express your perspective without sounding accusatory during these moments. Would you be willing to try one of these techniques in your next interaction?
“i” statements feel kind of fake, to be honest. like putting on a show. i just want to keep it real.

It makes total sense that you want to stay authentic rather than follow a script. Sometimes the goal is just to slow the reaction down without changing the words you use. Taking a physical pause before speaking can help you stay real while preventing escalation. Does that sound like something you could try next time?
it's not just me. her mood swings make everything escalate fast

It sounds like you feel her emotional shifts are driving a lot of the escalation. That can make it feel like you are walking on eggshells. Tracking what happens right before those shifts might help you navigate them. Do you see any specific patterns or triggers leading up to those moments?
i don't want to be tracking her like some project. just want to get through the day without another blow-up

It makes sense that you want to avoid conflict without turning her into a project. The most reliable control you have is your own response in the moment. Disengaging briefly can stop the cycle without requiring analysis. Does taking a short break feel doable for you?
part of me feels like walking away is just letting her win. but staying never helps either

It is very common to feel that stepping back means surrendering the argument. However, choosing not to engage is actually a way to protect the relationship from further harm. You are prioritizing long-term peace over winning a specific battle in the moment. Does viewing that pause as a strength help you feel more comfortable trying it?
maybe walking away isn't losing... maybe it's me keeping control

That is a really empowering way to look at the situation. Taking control of your own reaction often protects the relationship better than winning the argument. It puts the power back in your hands rather than letting the conflict dictate the outcome. Does that feeling of agency give you more confidence to try it next time?
what do i do when she blocks the door so i can't leave? that’s when it gets bad

It is deeply concerning that you are being physically blocked from leaving. If you feel you are in immediate danger, please call emergency services right away. For ongoing safety planning, I strongly encourage you to contact a local crisis line. Do you feel you have a safe place to go if this happens again?
it's not that bad. i just get loud, that's all

I understand why you might downplay it, but being physically blocked from leaving is a serious safety boundary. Feeling trapped often triggers louder reactions because the stress becomes overwhelming. Your physical safety needs to be the priority over staying in the room to finish the discussion. Does having a clear exit plan make you feel safer?
i'm supposed to be the strong one. not her. why can't i just keep it together?

It is exhausting to feel like you must be the strong one while dealing with such high tension. Getting loud when you feel trapped is a natural stress response, not a failure. Choosing to prioritize your safety in that moment is a powerful act of control. You don't have to carry that burden alone.
i hate that i yell at her... especially now, with the baby coming

It is understandable to feel regret about yelling, especially with a baby on the way. The stress of a new arrival can make even small conflicts feel much heavier. Acknowledging that you want to be better shows real strength. What kind of support do you feel you need right now to manage that stress?
i just need to get through this. don't need anyone else involved

I understand you want to handle this privately for now. However, physical safety for you and the baby must always be the top priority. If you feel trapped, removing yourself from the situation is the safest option. I am here to support you in finding ways to stay calm and secure.
it's just all piling up. i don't even know where to start fixing it

It is completely understandable to feel overwhelmed when so much is happening at once. Trying to fix everything at once can make the pressure feel even heavier. You might start by focusing on just keeping yourself safe in the moment. I am here to help you identify those small steps whenever you are ready.
it helps just saying it out loud, even a little

It is really good to hear that sharing this brings you some relief. Putting these heavy feelings into words can make them feel a bit lighter. You don't need to have all the answers fixed today. I will be here whenever you need to talk more.
